newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Network Peripherals pops.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Network Peripherals pops.

text.p: Options trading in Network Peripherals Inc rose sharply Friday as the stock rallied on heavy volume, traders said.
"The stock is going up for absolutely no reason and there's a lot of call buying," a trader at the Chicago Board Options Exchange said. "People are coming in to buy calls. It's all one-way."
He said talk on the floor was that the company would report sharply better than expected quarterly earnings later this month.
The options activity suggested some investors were looking for a takeover, the trader added.
The company said it would not comment on earnings or buyout rumors.
In afternoon trading, Network Peripherals shares were up 1-1/2 at 20 on more than 1.15 million shares. The stock reached a session high of 20-1/2, a level not seen since July 1995.
"The option doesn't trade frequently, but there's big order flow today and good size," a trader at the American Stock Exchange said. "There's significant retail demand for out-of-the-money calls.
"I don't know why and I don't know of any rumors or anything," he said of the increased options volume.
Calls that were out-of-the-money Thursday were at-the-money Friday. The highest strike available was 20.
Traders said volume in the Network Peripherals options began to increase Thursday, when around 900 contracts changed hands, compared to a daily average of around 50.
Volatilities rose in tandem with the pickup in volume.
"Volatilities mushroomed from around 50 to approximately 75 or higher now," the trader at the AMEX said. "Whatever it is, there's a lot of bullish speculation going on."
The trader in Chicago also said some put options were being sold, which also was consistent with a buyout.
The most active Network Peripherals option was the June 20 call, which traded about 440 contracts.
The March 20 call traded about 430 and the January 20 call traded roughly 365.
The most active put was the February 17-1/2, which traded 250 contracts.
